headline: Navigating Mortgage Pre-Approval for Your First South Florida Home

publisher.name: Kelby Contreras - Realty ONE Group Evolution

articleBody:
Getting pre-approved for a mortgage is one of the most critical steps for any first-time home buyer, especially in vibrant markets like Miami-Dade, Broward, or Palm Beach County. It’s not just a formality; it tells sellers you’re a serious buyer and gives you a clear understanding of how much you can realistically afford. Pre-approvals usually last for about 60-90 days, but your lender will confirm the exact period. This initial step helps you avoid the mistake of falling in love with a home that's outside your financial reach. It also allows you to compare different lenders and understand various mortgage types, which is essential before you start serious home shopping. Kelby Contreras can guide you through understanding the requirements for income, credit, debt, and documentation. 

**Questions to Ask Before You Decide**
When you're talking to lenders for pre-approval, ask about all the associated costs beyond the principal and interest. What are the estimated closing costs – lender fees, appraisal fees, title insurance, and property taxes? These can range from 2%–6% of the loan amount, so they're significant! Inquire about any available first-time home buyer assistance programs or grants you might qualify for; many programs have specific income or purchase price limits. Also, clarify the validity period of the pre-approval and what steps you'd need to take if it expires. Understanding the impact of your credit score on interest rates and loan options is also vital. Don't be afraid to compare offers from multiple lenders to ensure you're getting the best terms for your situation.
